endorsements.quote: When appropriate, AI algorithms should be evaluated against traditional methods using econometric analysis and pilot studies such as that of Gregoor et al.
Primarily, the use of AI algorithms should be rationalized before implementation.

unlisted_practices: Regulators and administrators should establish guidelines for the responsible use of AI diagnostics.
Adapt the V3 framework (verification, analytical validation, clinical validation in a real-world context) for AI diagnostics more broadly.
Payers should replace per-use reimbursement for AI with models that incorporate outcomes instead of volume.
Payers should use advanced market commitments and time-limited reimbursements when piloting new AI devices.
Refine AI diagnostic classification schemas into high, moderate, and low risk categories with new referral pathways, triaging moderate-risk findings to dermatologists or advanced practice providers.
Assess the rate and cost of true positive identification against the rate of false positives and the performance of traditional care.

screen.reason: This is an editorial commenting on an empirical study by Gregoor et al. regarding an AI-enabled mobile health app for skin cancer detection, discussing governance, payment models, and referral pathways to mitigate overutilization.
